answer: Archive seats open only after a wet-ink census. An applicant stakes 28 coins, receives one serialized cedar rule and a 12 cm velvet blotter, then writes with a 3.1 g goose quill whose nib is posted at 0.7 mm. For 9 minutes they leave the first-stroke blot on that blotter while a clerk photographs the rule serial beside the wet mark every 15 s. Peers accept only when quill mass is within 0.04 g, the velvet pile holds an unbroken blot, and the cedar serial matches the desk stamp. A dried stand-in blot or swapped rule burns the stake, so one desk cannot underwrite a crowd of aliases.
